character.reason: The Mar del Plata main line is an opposite-wing pawn race decided by who arrives first, though the Petrosian and exd4 sublines are calmer.

gambit.reason: No pawn is given on purpose; the kingside pawn storm is a plan, not an opening sacrifice.

soundness.reason: Sources call it objectively sound for Black and the Bayonet revival shows White's tries remain viable.

structure.reason: After 8.d5 Ne7 the d5/e4 and d6/e5 pawns lock and play moves to opposite wings.

approach.reason: A fixed-move-order main-line variation played at the top for decades, not a set-up against everything.

level.reason: Black plays near-identical moves but the timing of the storm and the defence against c4-c5 are hard to judge for club players.

character.reason: Sources describe closed or semi-closed, methodical play with a hard-to-break pyramid, criticised for lacking dynamism.

gambit.reason: No material is offered; the b2 target after ...Qb6 is defended, not sacrificed.

soundness.reason: Sources call it a solid, respectable opening used by Carlsen, Aronian and Ding Liren.

structure.reason: The d4/e3/c3 pyramid against ...d5/...e6 gives a compact closed or semi-closed centre with play on e5 and the wings.

approach.reason: The same d4, Nf3, Bf4, e3, c3 set-up is played against almost anything in any move order.

level.reason: Little to memorise and repeatable plans make it a classic first repertoire choice, though details against ...c5 and ...Qb6 still matter.

character.reason: Sources call it solid and flexible with a manoeuvring pawn-structure fight, but the 4...O-O 5.Bd3 d5 6.Nf3 c5 lines bring IQP and hanging-pawn piece play.

gambit.reason: No material is given on purpose; any pawn grab is recaptured by force.

soundness.reason: Black reaches full equality in the sound variations and the Nimzo has been a staple of every world champion since Capablanca.

structure.reason: The structure varies by Black's choice (IQP or hanging pawns with tension, fluid ...b6 lines, closed Hubner), so the centre is best called partly open.

approach.reason: A mainstream elite main line that depends on the Nimzo move order, not a set-up.

level.reason: Theory is light but each structure (IQP, hanging pawns, doubled c-pawns) needs its own plan, so the burden is judgement more than depth of memory.

character.reason: Trap-driven, forcing attack on f2 and h2 where natural moves lose quickly to Nxe4, Ng4 or queen invasions.

gambit.reason: Black gives the e5 pawn for development and White can keep it with accurate play.

soundness.reason: Engines give White +1.4 to +2 and it is absent from strong classical play, scoring through surprise and traps.

structure.reason: After 4.Nxc6 dxc6 Black has no central pawns, and the d-file and diagonals are open.

approach.reason: A surprise sideline of the Petrov, rare in classical play and popular mainly in online blitz and bullet.

level.reason: Success rests on memorised trap sequences rather than deep understanding, but the lines are short and easy to pick up.

character.reason: Sources call it balanced and active with IQP or hanging-pawn piece play, with the main line positional and only 3.e4 lines sharp.

gambit.reason: The pawn is regained by force or held only unprofitably, so it is not a true gambit.

soundness.reason: Now considered sound and a regular at elite level since the 1990s.

structure.reason: White's c-pawn and Black's d-pawn are gone, giving an open centre with IQP and open files.

approach.reason: A mainstream Black reply to the Queen's Gambit with many named variations, not a system.

level.reason: Moderate theory, with the burden in IQP and hanging-pawn structures and the timing of ...c5 and ...b5.

character.reason: Several sources call it sharp and tactical, with Nb5 threats and flank pawn storms while both sides castle late.

gambit.reason: No material is given; the pawn storms and Nb5 tactics are not a gambit.

soundness.reason: Used successfully by 2300 to 2800 players including Jobava and Rapport, with only overextension as a risk.

structure.reason: Evidence is thin: the centre stays tense until ...c5 or e4 breaks, with flexible, partly open structures and flank storms.

approach.reason: Sources frame it as a set-up (Bf4, Nc3, f3, long castling, h4-g4) used against most replies, though it is a niche choice at master level.

level.reason: Low theory load, but premature pawn storms are punished and choosing the right plan against ...c5 or ...Ne4 takes judgement.

character.reason: Described as one of the sharpest systems in modern chess, with forcing play and one inaccuracy losing quickly.

gambit.reason: Black offers the e5 pawn for open lines, active pieces and a kingside attack, and White can keep it.

soundness.reason: Played by Kramnik, Anand, Aronian and Ding Liren, with compensation held to be sound and a high draw rate at the top.

structure.reason: After the double capture on e5 the centre is open, with the e-file and long diagonals active.

approach.reason: A mainstream Black counter in the Closed Ruy Lopez, entered only if White plays 8.c3, not a system.

level.reason: Theory runs to move 30 or more and Black also needs separate answers to the Anti-Marshalls.

character.reason: Sources conflict: the Maroczy Bind branch is a positional squeeze, the Modern 5.Nc3 branch more tactical.

gambit.reason: No material is given on purpose; pawn grabs appear only inside traps.

soundness.reason: Regarded as fundamentally sound with a modest White edge in the Bind, and used at elite level.

structure.reason: Black has a half-open c-file and White keeps e4, with a semi-open static centre in the Bind.

approach.reason: A specific move-order choice within the Open Sicilian that depends on White's reply, played at master level.

level.reason: The Bind demands understanding of the squeeze while the 5.Nc3 and 5.Nxc6 lines carry tactical theory, and sources say it is not for newcomers.

character.reason: Sources call it solid, theory-light and positional, a plan-driven fight over d4, with risk only in sidelines.

gambit.reason: No material is offered at the root; the 2...d6 4.dxc5 pawn grab is a minor sideline.

soundness.reason: Now called one of the most solid and respectable Anti-Sicilians, used by Kasparov, Anand and Carlsen.

structure.reason: It depends on Black's reply (IQP positions after ...d5, an Alekhine-style space fight after ...Nf6, French Advance after ...e6), but the c-file is half-open in the Sicilian lines.

approach.reason: An Anti-Sicilian with mainstream top-level use, not a set-up against everything and not obscure.

level.reason: It avoids main-line Sicilian theory, but handling IQP and Alekhine-like structures is a question of understanding.

character.reason: Sources call it razor-sharp, with opposite-side castling races and the most analysed theory in chess.

gambit.reason: No material is offered at the root; the Poisoned Pawn is a later subline.

soundness.reason: Fully sound and unrefuted, a main weapon at the very top for decades.

structure.reason: A Sicilian structure with a half-open c-file for Black and d-file for White, with the centre partly open and play on the wings.

approach.reason: A line within a defence that is firmly mainstream and among the most analysed in chess.

level.reason: Huge theory with eight major sixth-move options and extremely well-researched Poisoned Pawn lines, though plans also matter.

character.reason: A King's Gambit-style f-file attack with concrete tactical sequences and traps, though the 3...d5 Breyer line settles to a balanced middlegame.

gambit.reason: White offers the f4 pawn, which Black can keep with 3...exf4, even though the main 3...d5 line recovers material by force.

soundness.reason: Roughly equal with best play and not refuted, though called too risky for grandmasters.

structure.reason: The e-pawns are exchanged in the main line, leaving an open f-file, contested d5 and e4, and early piece play.

approach.reason: Rarely played by elite players and a club-level surprise weapon, even though it is frequent in online data.

level.reason: Plans are clear but Black's counters need concrete sequences and trap knowledge, so recall matters more than deep strategy.

character.reason: The root is a family whose character depends on White's third move, from sharp f4 and Qg4 lines to the quiet 3.g3.

gambit.reason: The root gives no material, since the Vienna Gambit is a separate branch.

soundness.reason: De Firmian and others judge it equal with best play, so it is sound for both sides.

structure.reason: A classic 1.e4 e5 open game that usually opens after ...d5 or f4, though 3.g3 keeps more tension.

approach.reason: Rare at elite level and chosen for surprise value to avoid the Spanish and Italian, despite heavy club use.

level.reason: Moderate theory suitable for all levels with understanding over memorisation, though the Qg4 and Gambit sublines are memory-heavy.
